turns.content: Compare ethynylcyclohexane with the target aldehyde and identify the carbon-skeleton and functional-group changes the route must accomplish.
Explain why the alkyne reduction must stop at an alkene before the carbonyl-forming step.
Determine how to deprotonate the terminal alkyne established at the outset and install exactly one methyl group. Give the reagents and the resulting internal alkyne.
Choose conditions that reduce the internal alkyne only to an alkene, and justify why the reduction must stop there.
Choose a cleavage workup appropriate to the intermediate and target established above, and identify every carbonyl coproduct it would form.
Choose coupling conditions appropriate to the carbonyl species obtained in the preceding step without changing their required oxidation state, and explain the reagent's role.
Assemble the complete reagent sequence from the structural, reduction, cleavage, and coupling analyses already established.
Explain whether and why the reduction conditions chosen earlier stop at the required intermediate, and why that intermediate is necessary for the next step.
Use the carbonyl products and coupling analysis established above to explain which fragment supplies the target connectivity and why the smaller coproduct is not incorporated.
Report the four-step sequence and the purpose of each step.
